title: Two-Game and Five-Game Weeks: Lineup and Streaming Adjustments
brief: How should we adjust daily lineups, streaming adds (max 6 per week) and percentage-category expectations in weeks when a team plays only 2 or as many as 5 games? It must cover why low-volume weeks make FG% and FT% swing, why back-to-back counts matter little except for players returning from injury, and how merged NBA Cup weeks change the count.
summary: Games played is the schedule factor that matters in our 9-cat H2H league. A two-game week in the fantasy playoffs (weeks 19 to 21) is the one to plan around, so check it before the 2027-03-04 trade deadline. In low-volume weeks, treat FG% and FT% as coin flips and expect to win turnovers. In heavy weeks, use all 6 adds to stream for games. Back-to-back counts barely matter, except for players coming back from injury.

sections.heading: Why game count matters most in the playoffs

paragraphs.text: In head-to-head, the number of games your players log is a real edge. A player who plays only about two games in a week can cost you that week, even when his per-game numbers are good. He also holds a roster spot that could be used for streaming.

The schedule factor that actually matters is a two-game week in the fantasy playoffs. Our playoffs are weeks 19, 20 and 21, and the season ends 2027-03-28. If a player's team has a two-game week in that window, drop him down your board. Use the March 28 schedule, not Yahoo's April 4 default.

What to do: before the 2027-03-04 trade deadline, count each starter's games in weeks 19 to 21. Trade away a player with a two-game playoff week if you can get an equal player with a fuller schedule. After the deadline, the only fix is streaming.

sections.heading: Percentages and turnovers in light and heavy weeks

paragraphs.text: FG% and FT% are not safe in low-volume weeks. Fewer attempts means each miss moves the ratio more, so results swing more. FG% varies most from game to game and week to week. FT% varies most from year to year.

Shooting categories have no floor. One bad shooter can keep dragging the ratio down, and a lead can flip on the last day of the matchup. In a two-game week, do not count FG% or FT% as banked wins. Check both ratios on the final day before you set your lineup.

Turnovers work the other way. Being short on games, through injuries or a light schedule, lowers your turnovers on its own. So you often win TO in weeks when you have fewer games. In a heavy week where you stream for volume, turnovers will rise. Accept that. Chasing low turnovers fights the head-to-head game.
Heavy punt builds already run low volume and high variance. A two-game playoff week adds to that swing and can cost you. If you punt, be even stricter about avoiding two-game playoff weeks.

sections.heading: Daily lineups and the 6-add weekly cap

paragraphs.text: We set lineups daily and get 6 acquisitions per week, processed daily with FAB. Use all of them when you are chasing games. The end of the roster should keep turning over rather than sit still.

With 144 players drafted, players ranked around 170 to 190 are on waivers. Streaming them for extra games beats holding a player ranked around 130 who sits on your bench. Your 2 bench spots are the ones to churn. Drop a bench player whose team has a light week for a waiver player whose team plays more.
Good targets: backup centers who start when the starter sits, and bench players on teams with poor depth during heavy stretches when starters rest.

Time your adds for quality games. These are games on days with few NBA games, set at about 10 or 11 games or fewer, not Basketball Monster's default of 5. On those days you can start everyone without start/sit choices. A streamer whose games land on busy days may just sit on your bench.
Quality games are for in-season streaming, not for drafting. Season totals differ by only about six games between teams, which is too small to change auction prices on 2026-10-18.

sections.heading: Back-to-backs: small, except for returning players

paragraphs.text: Teams range from 13 to 16 back-to-backs across the season. That gap works out to about one game every two months, or about three over a 25-week season. Do not adjust draft prices or weekly plans for it.

The exception is a player coming back from an in-season injury. He may sit one game of a back-to-back, so a team with many back-to-backs hurts him more. Injury-prone players carry the same risk. Nobody can predict those injuries in advance. Check the schedule when the player returns: if his week has back-to-backs, count him for fewer games and stream around him.
One related flag: a long stretch of travel with no consecutive home or road games can wear a team down. That stretch is worth noting when you plan streams.

sections.heading: Merged NBA Cup weeks and early-season patience

paragraphs.text: The two NBA Cup half weeks, November 30 to December 13, merge into one 14-day matchup. Yahoo combines weeks seven and eight correctly this season. The All-Star weeks also merge. Count games across the full 14 days, not per half week. A team that is light in one half may be fine over the whole matchup. Your 6-add limit is a weekly cap, so check in Yahoo how it applies across the two-week matchup before you plan streams.

The experts disagree on how hard to chase games early in the season. One view says to stream for a games-played edge in head-to-head, since the waiver wire matters as much as the draft. The other says do not draft for the week one schedule and do not stream just for extra early games. In that view, losing weeks one and two is fine if it lets you hold fliers with longer-term value. For us: do not pay up in the auction for a good week one schedule. In weeks one and two, spend adds on evaluating players, not on streaming for games.
